newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea says to air 'important broadcast'.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea says to air 'important broadcast'.

text.p: North Korea's state-run radio said on Wednesday there would be an "important broadcast" later in the day.

The radio, monitored in Tokyo by Radiopress news agency one day after the formal end of the mourning period for the communist nation's founding father Kim Il-sung, gave no details of the content of the upcoming broadcast.
Radio Pyongyang and Korean Central Radio said there would be an "important broadcast" at 7 p.m. (1000 GMT) on Wednesday.
The announcement set off speculation that it could be a rare speech by Kim Il-sung's son and heir Kim Jong-il or a possible announcement of changes in the country's power structure.

Pyongyang announced on Tuesday the end of a three-year mourning period for Kim's father, "Great Leader" Kim Il-sung, paving the way for the son to take over the vacant posts of state president and general secretary of the all-powerful Workers' Party.
Korea watchers in Tokyo and Seoul have said Tuesday's ceremonies marked the formal start of the Kim Jong-il era.
But while Kim junior has been groomed for decades to step into his father's shoes, analysts say he is in no hurry to take charge while the country was in desperate straits.
Some analysts said Kim Jong-il was expected to take up the two leadership posts later this year, probably around the October 10 anniversary of the founding of the Workers' Party.
